clinical_safety.cohort: 66 treated participants with severe refractory gastrointestinal acute graft-versus-host disease
clinical_safety.adverse_events: 2026 follow-up reported 36 treatment-related treatment-emergent adverse events in 19/66 (29%). Sepsis, bacteremia, septic shock and gastrointestinal events were documented in an especially vulnerable patient population.
clinical_safety.serious_events: 2026 presentation: serious adverse events in 53/66 (80%); investigators considered eight serious events in seven patients treatment-related. Earlier ASH 2025 analysis reported 157 serious treatment-emergent events in 50/66 (76%).

clinical_safety.attribution: In the earlier ASH 2025 analysis, investigators deemed one fatal septic-shock event treatment-related. A death during the trial is not automatically caused by the microbiota treatment.
clinical_safety.limitations: The 26 fatal adverse events and 29 deaths are from different data cuts, not figures to be added. The single-arm high-risk population prevents causal interpretation of all-cause mortality without comparator/context.

clinical_safety.status: On-study deaths documented — not attributed to study drug
clinical_safety.trial: Historical SER-109 / VOWST ECOSPOR III (not a current Seres clinical pipeline program)
clinical_safety.cohort: Randomized trial: SER-109 n=90; placebo n=92
clinical_safety.adverse_events: SER-109 and placebo arms both had common treatment-emergent adverse events. Reported serious adverse events through week 8 were seven (8%) in the SER-109 arm versus fifteen (16%) in the placebo arm.
clinical_safety.serious_events: No serious adverse events in either arm were deemed related or possibly related to study product in the sponsor's reported tabulation.
clinical_safety.deaths: Three deaths occurred in the SER-109 treatment group; two had onset of fatal adverse events within the first eight weeks and the third later.
clinical_safety.attribution: Investigators considered none of the three deaths related to SER-109.
clinical_safety.limitations: Historical results for a previously developed product; the current company dossier lists different preclinical programs. Do not extrapolate the ECOSPOR III outcomes to those candidates.

programs.status_reason: 2025 peer-reviewed 15-participant study

programs.name: Hiltonol (poly-ICLC)
programs.indication: Innate immune activation in treated HIV; oncology vaccine-adjuvant programs
programs.phase: Randomized early clinical study; other investigational programs
programs.status_reason: 2019 randomized HIV study
programs.outcome: A small randomized trial documented transient immune activation and adverse events; serious events occurred only in the placebo group.

companies.mechanism: Hiltonol is synthetic stabilized poly(I:C), not bacterial material. It stimulates endosomal TLR3 and cytosolic dsRNA recognition, including MDA5, activating interferon-linked innate immune signaling. Biological effects can vary strongly with dose, route, disease, and combination therapy.
companies.clinical: In published studies, transient flu-like and injection-site reactions are common; rare grade 3 toxicities have been reported. Do not attribute combination-regimen events to TLR3 alone without investigator assessment.
companies.publication: 2025 Phase Ib study combining Hiltonol with oregovomab in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, and 2019 randomized poly-ICLC trial in treated HIV.
companies.patent: Investigational dsRNA immunomodulator. Patent search is not freedom-to-operate clearance.

patent_links.title: Search Oncovir poly-ICLC intellectual property
patent_links.note: Public patent discovery only

clinical_safety.status: Grade 3 thrombocytopenia probably related in one study; no AE-related deaths reported in that cohort
clinical_safety.trial: Hiltonol + oregovomab Phase Ib ovarian cancer (15 patients); separate poly-ICLC HIV randomized study NCT02071095 (12 active, 3 placebo)
clinical_safety.cohort: Ovarian: 15 heavily pretreated patients; HIV: 12 receiving poly-ICLC, 3 placebo. These are different trials and must not be pooled.
clinical_safety.adverse_events: Ovarian combination: flu-like symptoms and reported Grade 3 hypertension (2 patients), Grade 3 thrombocytopenia (1 patient). HIV study: injection-site pain, fever, myalgia and transient Grade 3 neutropenia (1 treated participant).
clinical_safety.serious_events: Ovarian Phase Ib: serious adverse events in 7/15 (47%); one Grade 3 thrombocytopenia was considered probably related to Hiltonol; other serious or severe events may reflect the combination or underlying disease. HIV study: two SAEs deemed unrelated, both in placebo recipients.
clinical_safety.deaths: Ovarian report: no adverse events resulted in death. This does not mean no patients died later from advanced disease. The cited HIV study did not establish a general mortality risk estimate.
clinical_safety.attribution: Study investigators judged the thrombocytopenia probably related to Hiltonol; other Grade 3 ovarian events were not uniformly judged related. The HIV trial's two SAEs were unrelated and occurred in placebo.
clinical_safety.limitations: Different routes, populations and treatments. TLR3 is not the only dsRNA sensing pathway engaged by poly-ICLC. These reports cannot establish safety across all poly-ICLC studies.

companies.mechanism: BO-112 is a synthetic poly(I:C) dsRNA nanoparticle formulated with polyethylenimine, not a bacterium or bacterial extract. It engages innate antiviral sensors, including TLR3 and cytosolic dsRNA sensing pathways, with tumor immune effects under investigation.
companies.clinical: Safety findings differ by route, indication and treatment schedule. Earlier severe thrombocytopenia reports and later no-SAE sponsor topline data represent different study populations, not contradictory findings.
companies.publication: 2020 first-in-human multicenter report and September 2026 Phase 2b SPOTLIGHT-204 sponsor-reported results.
companies.patent: BO-112 has product- and formulation-specific IP questions; public patent searches alone are not FTO opinions.

clinical_safety.status: Earlier Grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia reactions; no serious AEs in separate 2026 Phase 2b report
clinical_safety.trial: Phase 1 BO-112 NCT02828098; separate Phase 2b SPOTLIGHT-204 NCT06422936
clinical_safety.cohort: Phase 1 reported early monotherapy cohorts and a separate 28-person anti-PD-1 combination cohort; Phase 2b 2026 results reported 46 evaluable BCC patients out of 50 enrolled.
clinical_safety.adverse_events: Published Phase 1 report: two reversible grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia reactions. Phase 2b sponsor topline: 91% of treatment-related events were Grade 1 and most resolved rapidly.
clinical_safety.serious_events: In the September 2026 Phase 2b BCC dataset, the sponsor reported no serious adverse events and no treatment-related Grade ≥3 adverse events. This does not negate earlier Phase 1 thrombocytopenia reports.
clinical_safety.deaths: The cited 2026 topline report does not provide a complete all-cause death tally; no treatment-related fatality is established from the selected source materials.
clinical_safety.attribution: Phase 1 paper describes thrombocytopenia reactions during BO-112 treatment; Phase 2b sponsor explicitly reported no Grade ≥3 related events in that distinct trial.
clinical_safety.limitations: Different study designs, endpoints, patient populations, combination therapies and data cuts. Do not combine into a single pooled rate or imply pure TLR3-mediated causality.

companies.mechanism: Rintatolimod is a synthetic double-stranded RNA immunomodulator with a TLR3-focused mechanism. It is not a bacterial therapy and should be interpreted separately from poly-ICLC, whose cytosolic dsRNA sensing effects differ.
companies.clinical: In DURIPANC, the investigational combination includes anti-PD-L1 durvalumab, so immune-related AEs cannot be assigned to Ampligen alone without adjudication. Historical observational treatment differs from current prospective trial.
companies.publication: 2022 published observational rintatolimod pancreatic cancer program; November 2026 AIM announcement summarizing interim DURIPANC safety.
companies.patent: Synthetic dsRNA TLR3 agonist and combinations; patent-search leads are not clearance.

clinical_safety.status: Three Grade 3 immune-related AEs reported in combination DURIPANC interim update
clinical_safety.trial: DURIPANC NCT05927142, Ampligen + durvalumab; separate historical named-patient pancreatic program
clinical_safety.cohort: November 2026 company update: 28 enrolled across Phase 1/2; 2022 named-patient safety series is a separate cohort.
clinical_safety.adverse_events: Sponsor reported three Grade 3 immune-related adverse events during DURIPANC combination treatment. Named-patient study documented milder events but no grade 3–5 post-treatment events in its specified follow-up.
clinical_safety.serious_events: The available interim corporate report does not establish a complete independently audited SAE count for DURIPANC. A grade 3 immune-related AE is severe but does not automatically satisfy the regulatory definition of a serious AE.
clinical_safety.deaths: No complete verified all-cause trial death table or treatment-attributed mortality count was established in the reviewed interim reports; do not infer zero deaths.
clinical_safety.attribution: The DURIPANC combination includes durvalumab (anti-PD-L1). The three Grade 3 immune-related events cannot be attributed to TLR3 activation or Ampligen alone from this interim sponsor summary.
clinical_safety.limitations: Data are interim and sponsor-reported. Named-patient study lacked randomized control. Do not mix with other TLR3 agonists or different treatment populations.
